moduleTitle: Creating and managing teams of users
learningObjectives: Explain how the introductory Work Group model organizes cross-functional users around shared work
Distinguish a Work Queue (shared) from a Worklist (individual) and how Assignments move between them
Describe Work Group managers and Authorized Managers, including their limits

elements.description: A CROSS-FUNCTIONAL team — a manager plus a Work Queue — whose members share work regardless of their business unit. Note: an 'Operator' in Dev Studio is a 'User' in App Studio.

elements.text: Think of a project team drawing people from several departments, with a supervisor and a shared inbox. Team membership supports collaboration without reorganizing the company.

elements.term: Shared team queue and default queue
elements.description: The introductory Teams of users topic describes one shared queue for the team. Configuration uses a Default Work Queue field. Follow the documented setup for your version; do not infer additional queue or permission configuration solely from this simplified team model.

items: WORK QUEUE — a SHARED list for all operators in a Work Group
WORKLIST — holds only work assigned to ONE specific operator
An Assignment moves from the Work Queue to a Worklist when ready to be worked

elements.description: An operator must belong to AT LEAST ONE Work Group and can belong to MORE THAN ONE. Work Group membership controls work sharing without changing the organizational hierarchy. Configure users in App Studio; Dev Studio offers advanced options.

The linked configuration reference distinguishes access to a queue from processing work. If Roles are configured on that queue, processing requires at least one listed role. Team membership alone does not establish every permission.

elements.caption: The lesson model shows a manager, users with personal Worklists, and a shared team queue. Actual processing also depends on configured access.

elements.description: A Work Group names ONE operator as its PRIMARY manager. The system uses manager information for NOTIFICATION Tasks, APPROVAL Tasks, ROUTING Tasks, and ESCALATION. Managers assign, monitor, and report on the group's work using the Web Portal.
Authorized Managers assist with assignment transfer. This management relationship alone does not grant approval authority or unrestricted processing access.
items: They need not be members of the group.
The introductory source excludes approvals from these duties.
An authorized manager outside the group cannot complete its queued assignments under this lesson model.

elements.title: Worklist vs Work Queue Decisions

examPitfalls.title: Operator = User / people
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Operator and User are studio labels for the person record; the question must identify the studio rather than declaring one label universally correct.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the terminology for the studio specified.

examPitfalls.title: One Work Queue per Work Group
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The introductory topic describes a single shared team queue; the configuration procedure names a Default Work Queue.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Read the version-specific configuration rather than extrapolating from the diagram.

examPitfalls.title: Work Queue vs. Worklist
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks where assignments go when routed to an individual operator. Candidates say Work Queue. A Worklist belongs to one operator (personal queue); a Work Queue (Workbasket) is shared — routing to a named operator targets the Worklist.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Route to a Work Queue (Workbasket) for shared team pickup where any member can claim the work; route to a named operator for their personal Worklist only.

examPitfalls.title: At least one, possibly many
examPitfalls.trapDescription: An operator must belong to at least one Work Group and may belong to more than one; this does not change the org hierarchy.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Assign operators to Work Groups to enable shared work routing — an operator can belong to more than one Work Group simultaneously without organizational restructuring.

examPitfalls.title: Authorized Manager limits
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Authorized Managers transfer Assignments but CANNOT approve; if they are outside the Work Group they cannot complete Assignments from the Work Queue.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Transfer duties do not establish approval permissions.

examPitfalls.title: App Studio vs Dev Studio
examPitfalls.trapDescription: App Studio is recommended for routine user setup. Advanced configuration is documented separately; do not invent a bulk-management restriction from this topic.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Default to App Studio; use Dev Studio for advanced Operator/Work Group settings.

examPitfalls.title: Work Group vs. Access Group — different purposes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask how Work Groups and Access Groups differ. Candidates say they are the same. A Work Group organizes operators for routing and reporting; an Access Group grants access rights (Roles, Portals, Rulesets) — they serve completely different purposes.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Routing relationships and access permissions require separate configuration. Multiple Work Group memberships are supported.

examPitfalls.title: Work Group Manager is not an automatic approver
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks whether the Work Group Manager automatically becomes the approver for cases in that group. Candidates say yes. The Work Group Manager is an administrative role for the group — it does not automatically make that person an approver in any Case flow.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A management relationship does not configure every approval flow automatically.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A finance analyst, a marketing manager, and a staff writer in DIFFERENT business units all maintain the company website and must share a pool of work. What should the SA create?

options.text: A Work Group — a cross-functional team (with one Work Queue) whose members share work regardless of business unit
A new business unit that contains all three
Three separate Worklists that sync with each other
An Access Role shared by the three

practiceQuiz.hint: Cross-functional teams that share work assignments use a Work Group structure.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The team can collaborate across existing business units.

optionExplanations.A: The team can collaborate across existing business units.
optionExplanations.B: Reorganizing the business units is not required for this shared team.
optionExplanations.C: Separate personal lists do not express the requested shared pool.
optionExplanations.D: A role does not by itself establish this routing team.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the documented Work Group configuration, which field identifies the queue used as the group default?

options.text: Default Work Queue on the Work Group record
The operator password
The Case status label
The correspondence subject

practiceQuiz.hint: Look at the Work Group settings, not authentication or correspondence.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This is the named field in the documented configuration procedure.

optionExplanations.A: This is the named field in the documented configuration procedure.
optionExplanations.B: Authentication data does not identify the default work destination.
optionExplanations.C: A status label is not a queue reference.
optionExplanations.D: A message subject does not configure the team queue.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is explaining assignment routing to a client stakeholder who is designing team workflows. What is the key difference between a Work Queue and a Worklist in Pega?

options.text: A Work Queue is shared by all operators in a Work Group; a Worklist holds only one operator's work. Assignments move from the Queue to a Worklist when ready
They are identical; the names are interchangeable
A Worklist is shared; a Work Queue is personal
A Work Queue stores rules; a Worklist stores data

practiceQuiz.hint: Work Queue is a shared team list; Worklist belongs to one specific operator.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The shared pool and personal destination serve different routing needs.

optionExplanations.A: The shared pool and personal destination serve different routing needs.
optionExplanations.B: Interchanging the names loses the routing distinction.
optionExplanations.C: This reverses the personal and shared destinations.
optionExplanations.D: Both destinations hold assignments, not the stated rule/data split.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is onboarding a team of Claims Adjusters who handle both residential and commercial claims across two different departments, each with its own Work Queue. The SA must determine how many Work Groups a single operator can belong to in Pega.

options.text: At least one, and the operator may belong to more than one
Exactly one — operators cannot belong to multiple Work Groups
Zero or more — Work Group membership is optional
Exactly two — a primary and a backup

practiceQuiz.hint: Consider the minimum and maximum number of Work Groups an operator can belong to.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The topic permits multiple memberships with at least one required.

optionExplanations.A: The topic permits multiple memberships with at least one required.
optionExplanations.B: An exactly-one limit contradicts the documented membership model.
optionExplanations.C: The introductory model requires a group association.
optionExplanations.D: There is no primary-plus-backup numerical limit in this topic.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is setting up a Work Group for a loan processing team and is asked why the manager field is required. For what purpose does Pega use the Work Group manager's information?

options.text: Notification Tasks, approval Tasks, routing Tasks, and escalation — managers also monitor/report via the Web Portal
Only for sending marketing emails
To store the Ruleset version of the application
To authenticate operators at login

practiceQuiz.hint: Which four workflow functions rely on the Work Group manager's information in Pega?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Manager information supports configured supervision and workflow tasks.

optionExplanations.A: Manager information supports configured supervision and workflow tasks.
optionExplanations.B: Marketing correspondence is not the exclusive purpose of the relationship.
optionExplanations.C: Ruleset versioning is not stored by designating a team manager.
optionExplanations.D: Login authentication is not the purpose of this field.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega System Architect is explaining Authorized Manager capabilities to a BA who wants to understand how supervisors outside a Work Group can assist when the primary manager is unavailable. Which TWO statements about an Authorized Manager are correct?

options.text: They help transfer Assignments and can cover when the primary manager is unavailable
They cannot perform approvals
They must be a member of the Work Group
From outside the Work Group, they can still complete Assignments from the Work Queue

practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on what an Authorized Manager can do — coverage and transfer — and what they cannot do.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Assignment transfer is a documented assistance duty. The introductory topic excludes approvals from those duties.

optionExplanations.A: Assignment transfer is a documented assistance duty.
optionExplanations.B: The introductory topic excludes approvals from those duties.
optionExplanations.C: Membership is not required for this management relationship.
optionExplanations.D: Outside-group status does not confer queued-work completion authority.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA refers to an 'Operator' in Dev Studio. What is the equivalent term in App Studio?

options.text: A User (also called 'people') — the same record, different studio label
A Persona
A Work Queue
An Access Group

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the Dev Studio vs. App Studio terminology mapping for the same person record.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The labels depend on the studio used to manage the person.

optionExplanations.A: The labels depend on the studio used to manage the person.
optionExplanations.B: A persona describes a user category rather than this individual.
optionExplanations.C: A queue is a work destination, not a person record.
optionExplanations.D: An access group describes access configuration, not the person.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is setting up the very first Work Group and has not created a dedicated Work Queue yet. What can they use?

options.text: The default@pega.com Work Queue
No Work Queue — the first Work Group does not need one
A Worklist instead of a Work Queue
A temporary Data Page as the queue

practiceQuiz.hint: Hint: Pega provides a built-in default Work Queue you can reuse.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The topic explicitly permits the supplied default queue during initial setup.

optionExplanations.A: The topic explicitly permits the supplied default queue during initial setup.
optionExplanations.B: Initial setup does not remove the documented queue dependency.
optionExplanations.C: A personal list does not replace the shared team destination.
optionExplanations.D: A data page is not the documented queue configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team of 12 eligible operators should pull Claims Assignments from one shared pool. Which routing target expresses that requirement?

options.text: The Claims-Processing workbasket — routes to the shared queue where any of the 12 can pull work
The Work Group Manager worklist — the manager redistributes to team members
Round-robin assignment to each of the 12 operator worklists
Skill-match query returning the first available member across the 12

practiceQuiz.hint: For a shared team queue, route to workbasket or individual worklist?
practiceQuiz.rationale: This destination maintains the requested shared pool.

optionExplanations.A: This destination maintains the requested shared pool.
optionExplanations.B: Individual manager routing does not preserve that pool.
optionExplanations.C: Preassigning individuals differs from shared pickup.
optionExplanations.D: Selecting one individual differs from the shared destination requested.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the documented Work Group configuration, where are additional Authorized Managers listed?

options.text: Authorized managers on the Work Group tab
A Case status field
The correspondence template author field
An automatic Deputy Work Group Manager field required by this procedure

practiceQuiz.hint: The configuration procedure explicitly lists the optional manager entries.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The procedure specifies this optional manager list.

optionExplanations.A: The procedure specifies this optional manager list.
optionExplanations.B: A status value does not designate an additional manager.
optionExplanations.C: The template author does not establish this management relationship.
optionExplanations.D: The cited procedure does not require or document that invented field.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Routing resolves three Assignments to the same named manager, with no alternate routing configured. Which destination matches this individual routing?

options.text: The named manager’s personal Worklist
All three route to the Work Group workbasket, accessible by any member
Pega rejects the second and third because the WGM worklist holds only one active assignment
An automatic alternate manager destination solely because there are three Assignments

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish a personal destination from the shared pool.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Individual routing resolves to the named person’s destination.

optionExplanations.A: Individual routing resolves to the named person’s destination.
optionExplanations.B: A shared pool requires routing to the queue instead.
optionExplanations.C: The scenario supplies no single-assignment limit or rejection rule.
optionExplanations.D: The number of incoming tasks does not configure alternate routing.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Work Queue has a Roles restriction configured. A user can access the queue but has none of those roles. What requirement is missing?

options.text: At least one role listed in the Work Queue configuration
Exactly two Work Group memberships
A new Case title
The correspondence editor’s preview

practiceQuiz.hint: This question provides the actual configured restriction; it does not infer a cause from a missing button.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Processing requires at least one of the configured queue roles.

optionExplanations.A: Processing requires at least one of the configured queue roles.
optionExplanations.B: Counting group memberships does not satisfy the stated role restriction.
optionExplanations.C: Renaming a Case does not grant the required processing role.
optionExplanations.D: Email preview has no bearing on the queue role restriction.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is explaining how to structure a cross-functional team in a Pega application. Which TWO statements correctly describe a Work Group?

options.text: The introductory team model associates cross-functional users with shared work
A designated manager supports supervision of that team’s work
A Work Group stores individual Worklist assignments for each team member privately, separate from the shared queue
A Work Group must be associated with exactly one Persona or it cannot be created in App Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: A Work Group = team + shared Work Queue + manager — recall what it organizes and who manages it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Cross-functional work sharing is the team model’s purpose. The manager supports oversight of work performed by the team.

optionExplanations.A: Cross-functional work sharing is the team model’s purpose.
optionExplanations.B: The manager supports oversight of work performed by the team.
optionExplanations.C: Individual Worklists are not stored inside a group as claimed.
optionExplanations.D: This topic does not establish a mandatory Persona association.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements describe Authorized Managers in the introductory Teams of users topic?

options.text: They can assist with transferring Assignments
They are not required to belong to the Work Group
They automatically receive System Administrator permissions
Their designation automatically grants approval authority

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate transfer responsibilities and membership from permissions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Transfer assistance is a documented responsibility. The topic allows managers from outside the group.

optionExplanations.A: Transfer assistance is a documented responsibility.
optionExplanations.B: The topic allows managers from outside the group.
optionExplanations.C: The designation does not grant system administration rights.
optionExplanations.D: The introductory source explicitly excludes approvals from these duties.

quickRecap.value: Cross-functional team = a manager + one Work Queue; shares work across business units. (Operator = User/people in App Studio.)
The introductory team model has a shared queue; advanced configuration identifies a default queue.
Work Queue = shared team list; Worklist = one operator. Assignments move Queue → Worklist when ready.
At least one Work Group; may belong to more than one; does not change the org hierarchy.
One primary manager; drives notification/approval/routing/escalation; monitors via Web Portal.
Transfers Assignments / covers the primary; NOT required in the group; CANNOT approve; if outside, cannot complete Queue Assignments.
